newsitem.title: USA: Checkpoint sees Q1 and 1997 below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Checkpoint sees Q1 and 1997 below estimates.

text.p: Checkpoint Systems Inc said on Thursday that earnings and revenues for the first quarter and for 1997 would not meet analysts' expectations.

The company said that a combination of foreign currency fluctuations, the timing of some significant orders, and a one-time charge relating to Ultrak merger expenses will result in first quarter revenue of about $68 million and earnings per share of approximately $0.07, below what it said were analysts' estimates of $0.16 cents.
The company also estimated that for 1997, it will report revenues of about $325 million and earnings of about $0.67 per share, compared with estimates of $0.90.

A major reason for lowered expectations in 1997, the company said, was that its "comprehensive tag program", in which hardware is installed in stores at a small cost to the retailer in return for long-term label commitment, has the potential of becoming much more successful in Europe than the company anticipated.
This, said the company, will result in lower than anticipated hardware revenues in 1997, as those revenues are deferred and recognized over the term of the customer contract, usually five years.
